source: Ingested from savefromins.com  1 540P.MP4; timings measured with ffmpeg/whisper, roles and causal edges labelled by hand from the transcript.
note: Third reference and the shortest at 101s, well under the 170-220s the format bands were fitted to. Second reference for ACCUMULATING_INDICTMENT, so that engine is no longer defined by a single video.

observed.hook_type: Opens with a provocative counter-intuitive claim framed as 'explained like you're five', paired with a simple cartoon of two figures exchanging money while a wronged party walks away ignored, establishing the injustice immediately.
observed.story_pattern: Numbered step-by-step structure ('Step 1' through 'Step 5') that walks chronologically through a historical process, each step adding a twist or escalating scale, building toward a shocking modern-day connection.
observed.recurring_characters: Generic archetypes rather than named individuals: authority figures in period dress (suited officials, top-hatted men), an affected/wronged population, a board of decision-makers, and a modern presenter figure appearing near the end.
observed.location_reuse: Rotates through distinct illustrated settings — a symbolic doorway scene, a monumental government building, ornate wood-paneled council rooms, bustling document-processing halls, and a split-screen contrasting modern life with the historical past.
observed.visual_composition: Flat hand-drawn cartoon illustrations in muted sepia/pastel tones, alternating between wide crowd scenes, close-up single-character shots, and top-down/isometric bureaucratic tableaus to vary pacing.
observed.on_screen_text: A single large capitalized word from the narration is centered on each frame as a running caption, keyword-by-keyword, in bold white text with black outline.
observed.narrator_tone: Calm, explanatory, and matter-of-fact with a deliberate 'simplify the complex' teaching cadence, using understated framing to let the shocking facts land on their own.
observed.humour_and_interrupts: Dry ironic framing ('almost like an insurance claim'), casual asides that undercut the gravity, and the 'explained like you're five' conceit that lightens heavy subject matter.
observed.reveal_placement: The biggest gut-punch reveal — that the debt was still being paid off by ordinary people generations later, into the present era — lands in the final third right before the sponsor pivot.
observed.ending_callback: Abruptly transitions from the historical payoff to a sponsor pitch, branding the story as 'just one story inside' an app, comparing it to a popular learning app, and closing with a flattering call-to-action to try it.

story.title: America Freed the Slaves and Paid Their Owners Instead
story.start_state: slavery is still legal inside the nation's own capital

hook.line: America freed the slaves and paid their owners instead.

steps.label: April 1862, slavery legal in the capital
steps.situation: The Civil War is underway but slavery is still legal inside Washington itself, and Congress passes a law to end it there first.

steps.label: Lincoln signs it
steps.situation: Lincoln signs the law, and it reads as emancipation simply arriving.

steps.label: A board, and a petition to file
steps.situation: The government sets up a board of commissioners and invites loyal slave owners to file a petition for their loss of property.

steps.label: The injustice is treated as property
steps.situation: A government that ends an injustice by compensating the people who profited from it has priced the injustice as property rather than repudiated it.

steps.label: Three hundred dollars a person
steps.situation: For every enslaved person freed, the former owner is paid up to three hundred dollars.

steps.label: The freed receive nothing
steps.situation: Over nine months the board approves 930 petitions freeing nearly three thousand people, none of whom receive payment, land, or anything for their years of labour.

steps.label: A bonus for leaving
steps.situation: The law offers the owner a further hundred dollars if the freed person agrees to emigrate out of the country entirely.

steps.label: Britain had done it bigger
steps.situation: Britain had run the same arrangement thirty years earlier at vastly larger scale, paying its slave owners twenty million pounds, roughly forty per cent of the government's annual budget.

steps.label: Rolled into government debt
steps.situation: The sum was so large it was rolled into government bonds that ordinary taxpayers quietly paid off for generations.

steps.label: Not settled until 2015
steps.situation: The loan was not fully settled until 2015.

steps.label: People alive today paid the owners
steps.situation: People alive today, filing their taxes, were still making the payment to slave owners long after slavery itself had become ancient history.
